Holding a light takes a free hand and shows in first person; a two-handed weapon stows or drops it. Light, put out, drop, or throw torches; a thrown torch can ignite an enemy. Dropped torches persist across saves.
Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own horse art.

Your horse and wagon stay in the world, visible to other players online, and can follow, wait, or be called outdoors. Hitch them together, open a parked wagon from nearby entrances, and see its cargo and turning wheels.
Used with the author’s permission. The coastline is rebuilt from your own Daggerfall files.

Turns the Iliac Bay into a sea up to 250 meters deep where you can dive, swim, surface, and watch your breath. The depths hold underwater fog, seaweed, coral, fish, sea creatures, and guarded shipwrecks with treasure.
Used with the author’s permission, from the author’s MIT-licensed source, with the mod’s 210 sound clips.

Matches footsteps to surfaces (such as grass, gravel, snow, water, wood, and tile) and to leather, chain, or plate boots on stone. Also adds armor rattle, landing, and splash sounds in two quality levels.
Used with permission, on Mac’s word. The bundle names no author.
A card game of armies and kings played at tavern card tables against regulars or online against another player. Unit cards use art from Iliac Hand, and king cards use the Bay deck.
Uses {pack} for the original Daggerfall text, with permission from its authors.
Machine translation by Claude, checked and corrected by {names}.
Machine translation by Claude, still being checked. Corrections from native speakers are welcome.
Made for DFO and carried under the owner's exception for art drawn from Daggerfall's own (vendor/layered-armor/README.md).

Artwork for the Layered Gearing style, covering helmets, chest armor, leg armor, cloaks, and hoods for both body types. Includes leather, chain, and plate across seven metals, built from Daggerfall's class and enemy sprites.
Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Ralzar, authors Hazelnut and Ralzar).

Makes 20 monsters tougher and tones down rats, bats, and zombies. Werewolves and wereboars are a fifth larger, and the dragonling two and a half times its size. Based on version 1.5.2. With the combat overhaul on, Kirk.O's numbers apply.
Made for Bunnyfall by its owner.
The low-poly mine entrance placed at every mine mouth in the wilds, along with the ore and crystal models.
Used with permission, on Mac’s word, with its two tables carried byte for byte. The repository states no license.

Meaner Unleveled Daggerfall Enemy Expansion: Ralzar's Meaner Monsters balance patch for Daggerfall Enemy Expansion. When both are enabled, it rebalances 35 classic and expansion monsters and gives each dungeon type themed, unleveled encounter tables.
Used with the author’s permission, on Mac’s word. The archive states no license and names no author.

An optional leveling mode, offered at character creation, from an OpenMW Lua mod for Morrowind. Skills fill a 100-point bar, fastest for primary and major skills, and overflow carries over. Each level gives points for attributes, with Luck costing more.

Adds deep-sea blue holes to Iliac Puddle No More, marked by dark pits under plumes of miasma. Swim down to enter flooded, pitch-black dungeons where sea creatures replace fire enemies and loot rolls one material tier higher.
Used with the author’s permission. Based on the released mod and its public source, which states no license.

Armor reduces damage instead of hit chance, and skills and stats decide hits and blocks. Wear uses his Believable Equipment Characteristics And Durability. His versions of Ralzar's Meaner Monsters and Roleplay & Realism's archery apply when those mods are on.
Not distributed with the game. Each player supplies their own copy.
Hand-drawn paperdolls for female characters, loaded from your own copy of the mod (none of its art ships with the game). Any missing metal variants are recolored from the mod's existing sprites.
The game's own work (vendor/pixelify-glyphs/, built by tools/pixelifyGlyphs.py).
Custom 2 and Z glyphs drawn on the Pixelify Sans grid for the Enhanced skin so they cannot be mistaken for each other.
Made by Kamer for this game, used with his permission, with some bugs fixed.

Knights, bandits, or orcs raid towns daily for 2 hours (10 real minutes online). Defeat 15 to 25 raiders with the watch to raise standing with the region, its people, a knightly order, and the Fighters Guild.
The author’s own work, from his repository.
An animated leather book reader for the Enhanced skin with an opening cover, two-page spreads, turning pages, and stained paper. It displays Daggerfall's books in their original fonts.
Free to edit and redistribute, as long as credit to the original creator is included.
Ten new Argonian heads and bodies for both genders, with a matching vampire face for each head. Available as Argonian faces 11 to 20 alongside the original ten.
Used with the author’s permission under the MIT License.

Gameplay rule changes such as bow draw power, climbing, swing speed, armor wear, encumbrance, loans, ship boarding, and usable beds. Also includes NPC variants, enhanced riding, refined training, and the Master Armorer quests.
Used with the authors’ permission under the MIT License. The 280 sprites are the authors’ own art.

Adds the Archer's Axe, the Light Flail, and light and medium armor sets in every metal with custom art. Also rebalances item weights and prices, and updates loot tables, enemy gear, starting kits, and shop stock.
Autumn, spring, and winter textures for trees, rocks, and plants in woodland, hill, haunted, and mountain regions. The textures are not bundled and load from your own copy of the mod.
Used with the author’s permission, with the mod’s own 600 sprites.
Renders your shield in first person with metal-matched sprites that show wear as condition drops. The shield bobs as you walk, slides away when you sheathe, swing, or cast, and recoils when struck.
SIL Open Font License 1.1. The license is included with the glyph.
Provides the digit 5 for numbers in the Enhanced skin, replacing the Pixelify Sans 5 that resembles an 8.
Code under the MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Hazelnut, PlayerAutoPilot Copyright (C) 2019 Jedidia). The 3 interface textures are the mod’s own art, used with the author’s permission.

Adds accelerated overland travel with steering controls, encounter stops, and following Basic Roads' roads and tracks, using Jedidia's Tedious Travel autopilot. Also adds a road-network map overlay, a ports filter, a location info key, and location markers.
Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (C) 2020 Ralzar).

Loot and stock ignore your level; materials follow luck, shop quality, and dungeon type. Bodies carry gold divided by your level and multiplied by luck. Daedra and Orcs can drop their metals, and any material can stand in for another.
From vgmstream’s table (ISC-style license) and libvorbis’s encoder output (BSD-3-Clause, Xiph.org). Both licenses are included with the files.
Restores two Vorbis setup headers that Unity audio clips omit, so Come Sail Away’s five sounds play as the author made them.
Used with the author’s permission. The quests are his own, unchanged, and the ships are his edits applied to your own game files.
Adds pirate ambushes during ship fast travel, where you and your crew fight raiders on deck to reach your destination. Includes his four quests and six ship layouts.
The mod’s own permission: free to use with credit and no fee.

Sheathed Morrowind weapons hang in scabbards and quivers: 71 models and 3 skeleton add-ons that work as in OpenMW. Scabbards by akortunov, Greatness7, Heinrich, London Rook, Lord Berandas, Melchior Dahrk, MementoMoritius, Petethegoat, PikachunoTM, and Remiros, per the readme.

Overhauls first-person weapons and Morrowind arms with wind-up and recovery animations, active-hand rendering, and smooth sheathing. Adds walking bob, look inertia, double-size idle sprites from the mod, and recoil when you hit, parry, or miss.
Not distributed with the game. Each player supplies their own copy.
Optional art and townsfolk loaded from your own copy of the mod, with no assets bundled with the game. The Dibellan Degeneracy add-on has its own switch.

Adds windmills at the seven farms the author chose, on the Enhanced skin, with turning sails, interior machinery, and 17 climate and seasonal variants. The Classic skin keeps Daggerfall's original farms.
Used with the author’s permission, confirmed by Mac.

Populates 227,938 wilderness squares across the Iliac Bay with his 65 layouts of bandit camps, forts, ruins, shrines, mountains, and rock fields. Includes the bandits, bears, warriors, and treasure they hold, plus his camp outside Privateer's Hold.
Used with permission under its MIT License (Copyright (c) 2009-2018 jefetienne), with a second MIT notice for Daggerfall Workshop.

Press Jump at ledges to vault or hang (Left and Right shimmy, Forward climbs up, Crouch lets go). Hold Forward on walls to climb. Your Climbing skill sets grip, reach, and speed, and Off keeps classic climbing.
Shows visual cues for concealed enemies without changing combat rules: chameleons shimmer, shadows become silhouettes, and invisible enemies flash when hit. Off keeps them hidden.

Adds a dynamic sky with sun, moons, stars, weather clouds, rain, snow, and windblown grass. Off restores the classic sky, while the third option enables Dynamic Skies by BadLuckBurt and carademono, whose settings open on this tile.
Lighting changes when the world next loads. Steady shadows and calmer eye change right away.

Adds dynamic torch and sun shadows, glowing windows, fog light, darker corners, and sunbeams, while Off uses classic flat lighting. Steady shadows reduces shadow flicker at some cost to frame rate, and Calmer eye slows brightness adaptation.
Combines the world, towns, and dungeons into one handheld parchment map that you can pan and zoom. Off uses the three classic map windows.

Adds ambient and action audio to the enhanced UI, including dynamic wind, coins, climbing, gathering, horses, and ships at sea. Also adds shoreline surf, regional wildlife by time of day, and town streets, smithies, and taverns.
Gives seas, rivers, and ponds clear water with wind-driven waves, shore foam, movement ripples, and sky reflections. Off restores the classic flat water.
Lists active world events on the left with distance, time left, and updates saved to your journal. You can dismiss single events, or turn the board Off to show updates in chat and HUD messages.
Applies local lighting to your first-person weapon, spellcasting hands, off-hand torch, and Morrowind arms.
The amount changes when the world next loads. The style changes right away.

Requires the Improved Interior Lighting mod. Its warm, flickering lights replace the classic lighting, and with shadows on, lamps, people, and monsters cast soft shadows too.
With the Morrowind body, characters and horses appear as flat camera-facing sprites, like the classic sprites. When off, they render in full 3D.
In third person, the Morrowind body matches your movement speed, holds each weapon differently, and swings with its whole body while moving. When off, it uses Morrowind’s original animations.
With the Morrowind body, Pixelated draws characters, horses, and your arms in large pixels like the classic sprites. Sharp draws them at full screen resolution and uses more video memory.

Takes effect right away. Ship handling changes the next time you take the helm. Online it’s always on.

Fight pirates, merchants, and navies on Come Sail Away ships. At the helm, look to a side, hold Attack to aim, and release to fire. Board surrendered ships for cargo. Piracy is a crime, and pirates can board you.
The screen pulses as your health gets low: slowly below 40%, fast below 20%. On by default in Daggerfall Unity.
With Morrowind People on, floating icons mark key townsfolk. Quest targets show a yellow mark, merchants show a coin, and guild trainers, guild quest givers, and arena officers show a blue gem.
Shows an on-screen notice when a quest starts or ends, adds a journal entry, or has less than a day left. When off, the journal updates without a notice.
Marks known quest destinations on your map and shows your tracked quest on the compass. When off, the map and compass show no quest markers.
A top-right card shows your tracked or most recently updated quest, including its latest entry, destination, and time left. When off, no quest card is shown.
Takes effect on the next quest you take. Quests you already have keep their rules.

Quests show their objectives, some offer ending choices or fitted gear, and questlines lead to the Breaches, the Battlespire, and the Abyss. When off, quests use the classic journal and rewards (always on online).

Loot without opening a window: scroll with the mouse wheel, press Activate to take one item, or use Take everything. Take everything skips junk (filtered by Take gear), and turning this off uses the inventory window.

Diamond shows 4 bottom-left slots (keys 1–4), and Hotbar and Diamonds show 10 above your health bars (keys 1–0). Drag items or spells onto slots, or hover and press a key. Off hides them, but keys still work.

Trees cluster into forests with open grassland between them, hiding dungeons, ruins, shrines, and camps while leaving towns and farms in clearings. Deserts are unchanged, and turning this off spreads trees evenly like the original.
Renders the world at a lower resolution while keeping menus and the HUD sharp. Try 75% if outdoor areas run slowly on high-resolution screens (overridden while Retro Picture Mode is on).
Highlights nearby herbs, veins, trees, and other gathering spots. Glint adds a sparkling shimmer, Outline draws a colored rim by profession visible day or night, and Both combines them.
Takes effect on the next dungeon you enter. Loading a save from the other size places you at the dungeon entrance.

Shrinks large dungeons to five blocks (one center block with four around it), while main-story dungeons stay full size. Active quests keep their original dungeon size, and online dungeons each use their own fixed size.
Takes effect right away. New characters and shop stock follow it.
Dungeon light comes from torches, lanterns, or candles you carry that burn down over time, instead of a permanent light. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.
If a monster attacks you in town while you are not wanted, guards come to help and leave once it is safe. Guards still pursue you for crimes, and when off, they appear only for crimes.
Random monsters are picked from the dungeon’s full list around your level, so a dungeon has more variety instead of the same few. Off by default in Daggerfall Unity.
Takes effect at once. Online, each player picks their own.
Wagons wear down during travel and can be mended at a Wagon Yard or with a Wagon Repair Kit. Boons has no wear penalty, Hard makes worn wagons slower and worth less, and Off disables wear.
How detailed the enhanced water is. Full shows what lies under the surface and ripples where things move. Simple is lighter on your machine.
Weapons with fire, frost, or shock bonuses show a moving elemental outline that brightens with strength, and enchanted Morrowind weapons glow. When off, weapons appear without glow effects.
Rain, storms, and snow move across the land with the wind, so you can see a storm coming and walk through it. When off, classic weather applies uniformly across the region.
In the wilds, you can encounter enemy camps and roaming packs instead of only single enemies at a time. When off, wilderness encounters spawn one enemy at a time.
Makes wind visible in the enhanced outdoors: trees and plants lean and sway, and faint air streaks show its direction and strength.
